title: release-rollout-scratchpad-harper-wells
content:
Goal: sketch a safe canary rollout for runtime v2.3.1 -> shipping to hosted and dedicated for Jan patch window. Quick notes / TODOs / checklist for myself (Harper).

High-level rollout plan (working):
- Stage 0 (preflight): internal canary on staging cluster, smoke tests. Must pass: model load, KV cache priming, streaming handshake.
- Stage 1 (internal canary): 1% traffic to new runtime in prod region us-west1, alpha customers only (internal flag). Run for 2 hours at minimum with continuous monitoring.
- Stage 2 (progressive ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24-48 hours, only if metrics stable.
- Stage 3 (full): 100% if no regressions and SLOs met for 72 hours.

Version pinning notes:
- Customers pinned to model-serving-version=stable-2.3.0 will not get 2.3.1 unless explicitly opted-in. For Dedicated customers on reserved clusters, ops will schedule patch windows; notify account owners.
- Ensure runtime compatibility matrix updated in repo and confluence before pushing. Tag release in repo: runtime-v2.3.1-canary.

Must-watch metrics (primary):
- p50/p95/p99 token latency (streaming and non-streaming) by route
- error rate (5xx) and grpc statuses (if applicable)
- model load failures / OOMs per host
- token throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU pool
- failure modes: stale KV cache misses spike, unexpected duplication of tokens
- cost signals: GPU utilization drop/increase relative to baseline
- user-visible regressions (quality): random sample of outputs via eval set (run eval job every hour)

Automated checks (pre-deploy):
- unit + integration tests passing on CI (runtime + deployment templates)
- benchmark: perf-run vs baseline; must be within +-10% p95 latency
- smoke script: run 500 short-context prompts + 100 long-context, assert no OOM and responses complete within 2x baseline latency

Canary rollback criteria (any of the following triggers immediate rollback to previous version):
- p95 latency > baseline_p95 * 1.25 for >30m
- error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points and sustained >15m
- any model load OOMs on >1 host in pool
- user-facing incident reported in #prod-ops Slack channel with severity >=medium
- automated eval quality score drop >5% on canary eval suite

Runbook snippets / operator steps:
- To promote from N% -> M%: update rollout policy in console (route weight) or run infra script: scripts/rollout/update_weight.sh --from 1 --to 5 --region us-west1 --release runtime-v2.3.1-canary
- To rollback: scripts/rollout/rollback.sh --release runtime-v2.3.0 --all-regions (this forces route switch, drains new pods)
- After rollback: open incident ticket JIRA-3412 and paste logs + metric diffs; notify affected customers.

Observability checklist (must be green before each step):
- Dashboards: canary-runtime-latency, canary-error-rate, canary-deploy-health visible and pinned to channel
- Alerts: p95 latency alert configured for canary namespace with 5m window; index is set to notify on-call SRE
- Tracing: ensure trace sampling for canary traffic is 5% (higher than prod default) to debug tail latency

Communication plan:
- Pre-rollout: post in #prod-ops and #releases with ETA, impacted regions, and roll plan (timeboxed)
- On each promotion step: update thread with metrics snapshot + decision rationale
- Post-mortem: if rollback happened, capture root cause within 48 hours and circulate to eng + product

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Should we gate 50%->100% on qualitative eval from a human reviewer for hosted API? Asking Maya.
- Check if Dedicated customers with custom kernels require special packaging; ping infra team.
- Confirm SRE on-call availability for launch window (date TBD) - put a calendar hold once date confirmed.

Quick checklist (tick off during rollout):
- [ ] Tag release in git and attach changelog
- [ ] Bump canary flag in console and set weighting plan
- [ ] Run preflight perf-run and smoke tests
- [ ] Notify channels and update on-call
- [ ] Promote 1% internal canary -> wait 2h -> validate metrics
- [ ] Ramp -> run hourly evals and maintain log of snapshots
- [ ] Final promotion and close release ticket

Notes to self: keep logs of small regressions (even if under thresholds) - they matter for post-release tuning. Save eval outputs to s3://redwood-release-evals/2025-01-runtime-2.3.1-canary/ for quality runbook.

Snippet of useful commands to paste elsewhere:
- Promote traffic: curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' "https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/promote" -d '{"release":"runtime-v2.3.1-canary","region":"us-west1","weight":5}'
- Fetch canary metrics: ./scripts/metrics/fetch.sh --namespace canary-runtime --window 60m --metrics latency,error_rate,ooms

End of scratchpad. Will refine after talking with Maya/Jordan and SRE.
